$comment: CHART RENDER DETERMINISM - every Application rendered TWICE and compared.
Written by `bun src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/chart-render-determinism.ts --measure`;
checked by the same file with no flag. Do not hand-edit: re-measure.
A chart whose render differs from ITSELF is non-deterministic by construction.
ArgoCD diffs a fresh render against live state on every sync, sees a difference
that is not a drift, re-applies, and under selfHeal the workload churns forever
- on any cluster, including the one that boots off the USB installer.
== THE FOUR ROWS, AND WHAT EACH ONE NEEDS ==========================
regenerated-secret  the chart mints a password or certificate at TEMPLATE time.
Remedy: supply the value (existingSecret, a pre-created
Secret, an external-secrets reference) so it stops inventing
one. cilium (CA + two hubble cert pairs), seaweedfs (sftp),
weaviate (cluster-api basic auth).
fresh-identity      a hook/test Pod whose NAME carries a random suffix. Remedy:
exclude the hook from the render, or accept it via
ignoreDifferences. Nothing about its contents is wrong.
gitlab (webservice test runner).
contents-differ     anything else. No instance today; kept so a NEW shape is
reported rather than bucketed into one of the two above.
== WHY fresh-identity ROWS CARRY A `*` =============================
Their whole defect is the random suffix, so a literal name here would make THIS
FILE non-deterministic - it would go red against the next run of the same tree,
which is the failure the row exists to record. The suffix is derived by
COMPARING the two renders' names, never guessed from one of them: the first
version guessed, required a digit, and missed `jjcvk`.
NAMED, and never counted as stable: an app nobody can render has not been shown
to be deterministic. It is EMPTY today, and it was six an hour before this file
existed - arc-controller, argo-rollouts, argocd, cloudnativepg, external-secrets
and kube-prometheus-stack all reported `helm-template-failed` with an EMPTY
detail. Running helm by hand on cloudnativepg exited 0 and produced 1,272,266
bytes: the failure was OURS, a 1 MiB spawnSync maxBuffer in defaultRunHelm, and
the reason was lost because spawnSync leaves stderr as the empty string on that
path so the `??` fallback never reached error.message. Both halves are fixed.
Six charts that 'could not be rendered' were six charts nobody had rendered.
stable + unstable + unmeasured always equals appsDiscovered; a test asserts it.
